legend: A grasshopper starts at position 0$$$0$$$ on a number line containing the points 0,1,2,…,n$$$0, 1, 2, \dots, n$$$.

Each minute, the grasshopper chooses a point j∈{0,1,…,n}$$$j \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}$$$ that it has not chosen before and jumps over it. If the grasshopper is currently at position i$$$i$$$ and jumps over point j$$$j$$$, it lands at position 2j−i$$$2j - i$$$.

After exactly n+1$$$n+1$$$ minutes, the grasshopper has jumped over every point 0,1,…,n$$$0,1,\dots,n$$$ exactly once. It is guaranteed that after all jumps, the grasshopper returns to position 0$$$0$$$.
Your task is to count how many permutations of the jump-over points result in this behavior.
input: The first line contains an integer t$$$t$$$ — the number of test cases.
Each of the next t$$$t$$$ lines contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤75)$$$(2 \le n \le 75)$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of all values of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 75$$$75$$$.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the number of valid orders of jump-over points modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.
note: Each point from 0$$$0$$$ to n$$$n$$$ must be jumped over exactly once.
The order of jump-over points matters.
Some values of n$$$n$$$ may have zero valid permutations.
Since the answer can be large, all results are taken modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.
For example, when n=4$$$n=4$$$, one valid order is: [ 0, 1, 2, 4, 3 ] After performing these jumps, the grasshopper returns to position 0$$$0$$$.
